title: A surprise party: Maya and Ben make plans

script.text: Ben, thanks for coming. I wanted to talk about Lucy's party before the others arrive.
Sure. Her birthday is on the twenty-first, right? I thought we'd just go out for pizza.
That's what I'd planned originally, but then her sister told me Lucy is expecting exactly that, so there wouldn't be any surprise.
Fair point. What's the new idea?
Her aunt has a garden house just outside town. It's empty in October, and she says we can use it for free, as long as we clean it afterwards.
Free is good. Is it big enough?
For about twenty people. I've counted: there'll be fifteen if everybody from her class comes, plus a few from the swimming club.
What about getting there? It's not on a bus route, is it?
There's a bus until six, but after that, nothing. My dad has offered to drive some of us in his van, and I'm sure other parents will help.
Brilliant. And food?
That's your department, I thought. You're the one who made that enormous chocolate cake for the school fair.
Ha! It collapsed halfway through the fair, you know. But I'll try again with a different recipe. Should I do a cake with candles, or is that too childish?
She'll love it. Her favourite is lemon, by the way, not chocolate, so keep that in mind.
Lemon. Noted. What about music? I could bring my speakers.
Tom has promised to put together a playlist, but the speakers would be useful, because the ones in the house are ancient.
No problem. How are we going to get Lucy there without her suspecting?
Her sister will tell her that the family are going for a walk in the countryside. When they arrive at the garden house, all of us will be hiding inside.
And if she guesses?
She won't. She guessed last time because somebody posted a photo online, so I've asked everybody not to put anything on social media until the party is over.
Sensible. Are we buying a present together?
I'd like us to give one big present rather than twenty small ones. I'm thinking of a good camera, since she's always wanted to take up photography. We'd need about eight pounds each.
That's fine. I'll collect the money from the boys.
Thank you. I'll send everyone the details this evening.

statements: Maya had first intended to celebrate Lucy's birthday with a pizza meal.
Lucy's aunt expects to be paid for the use of her garden house.
Every guest can reach the garden house by bus.
Ben has previously baked a cake for a school event.
Lucy's family are planning a separate dinner on the day of her birthday.
The guests are going to give Lucy several small gifts.
Tom will play the music at the party himself.
discuss: Have you ever organised a surprise for someone? What happened?
How do you usually celebrate your birthday? Would you like a surprise party?
Is it better to give one big present from a group or many small ones?
